newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan ends down slightly vs US dollar in Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: Yuan ends down slightly vs US dollar in Shanghai.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed down slightly at 8.2908 against the U.S. dollar on Thursday due to a technical correction after it hit a two-year high on Wednesday, traders said.
The weighted average price on Wednesday was 8.2910.
Dealers said profit-taking set in after the yuan failed to breach the key 8.2900 resistance level early in trading.
The yuan opened higher at an intraday high of 8.2900 and fell slightly to move around 8.2910 for most of the session, hitting a low of 8.2911.
Trading was dull with most business down at 8.2909.
One dealer said profit-taking prevented the yuan from rising further despite its higher opening on Thursday.
A second dealer said the yuan failed to end up mainly because it failed to breach the psychologically-important 8.2900 level, which dampened pro-yuan sentiment.
"But the yuan had strong support at the 8.2910 level," he said. "The balance of selling and buying made it move in a narrow range."
Dealers said they expected the yuan to move around the 8.2910 level on Friday.
The yuan closed up at 7.2518 from 7.2950 against 100 Japanese yen and little changed at 1.0695 from 1.0696 against the Hong Kong dollar.
